title: Human-in-the-loop validation
task_statement: Place human approval and review where the stakes require it, with full decision context. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Pre-action approval for irreversible actions
components.first_principle: A person approves an action before it runs when the action cannot be undone.

nodes.label: Managed Agents session paused for approval

steps: Set the permission policy to always_ask for each tool that moves money or changes data.
The session pauses with stop_reason requires_action and waits for a user.tool_confirmation event.
Show the reviewer the tool arguments, the policy, and the sources. (Inference)
The reviewer sends allow or deny for each blocked tool call.
The tool runs only after an approval.
Record the decision, the reviewer, and the arguments. (Inference)
pros: Stops an irreversible action before it runs.
Uses a native pause in Managed Agents, so the session waits for the answer.
Gives an audit point for each decision.
cons: Reviewer latency slows each action that waits for an answer.
A tired reviewer can approve a call without a real look at the context. (Inference)
A review without context is not a real check. (Inference)
use_when: An action moves money, deletes data, or changes access.
A policy names a person as the approver. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: The action is read-only and public.
Volume is high and each action is reversible. Use sampled review instead. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Require approval for each action that cannot be undone.
constraints.combination: Name the approver role in the policy record. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Accept the pause for irreversible actions only.
constraints.combination: Use post-action review for reversible actions.
List idle sessions on a schedule, because a webhook delivery can be missed.

constraints.choice: Set always_ask only on the tools that need approval.

components.exam_tie: D5.3. Expect a scenario where an action is irreversible and costly. The credited answer places approval before the tool runs. (Inference)
components.trap: Approval on every action, even at high volume, which stalls the queue. The stakes decide the review shape.
components.decision_rule: Use pre-action approval when the action cannot be undone.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario gives a volume and a cost per review, compare the review load before you choose a shape.

key_facts.text: Manual mode asks before most actions that edit files, run shell commands, or reach the network.

key_facts.text: A session whose stop_reason type is requires_action needs your answer.

components.name: Post-action review and monitoring
components.first_principle: A reviewer checks what ran after the fact, and a tested rollback path undoes a reversible action.
steps: Subscribe to webhooks for sessions that go idle or reach a budget.
Verify the signature on each webhook delivery.
List idle sessions on a schedule, because a delivery can be missed.
Run an offline reviewer job that reads each session's events.
Send each flagged action to a human reviewer.
Undo the action with a rollback procedure that you tested before the run. (Inference)
pros: Covers reversible actions at a low review cost.
Finds behavior beyond the granted tools with an offline job.
Reports idle and budget events through webhooks.
cons: Post-action review does not stop the first action.
A rollback that does not work turns the review into a report. (Inference)
use_when: The action is reversible and the rollback is tested.
Sampling finds problems across many sessions.
An audit needs a record of what the agent did.
do_not_use_when: The action moves money or deletes data with no undo.
One error would cause harm before a sample reaches a reviewer.

constraints.combination: List sessions on a schedule to catch missed webhooks.

constraints.choice: Keep session events for the period that your audit requires.
constraints.combination: Copy session events to your own logs before you delete a session.

constraints.choice: Sample sessions at a random rate for the offline review.
constraints.combination: Raise the sample rate after errors appear. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Give the reviewer job read access to events only.

native_services.text: Claude in Amazon Bedrock emits logs to CloudWatch and CloudTrail. Anthropic recommends a 30-day rolling retention of activity logs.
The Admin API offers telemetry destination endpoints on this platform.

components.exam_tie: D5.3. Expect a scenario with many reversible actions. The credited answer samples or reviews after the action, with a rollback path. (Inference)
components.trap: Post-action review presented as protection for an irreversible action. The review runs after the harm.
components.decision_rule: Review reversible actions after they run, and keep a tested undo path.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario says the action cannot be undone, choose pre-action approval.

components.name: Hook-based approval point in Claude Code
components.first_principle: A PreToolUse hook runs code before a tool call, so a team can add a custom check that the rules cannot express.

edges.label: tool input as JSON on stdin

steps: Claude Code sends the tool input as JSON on stdin to the hook.
The hook checks the command or the arguments against your policy.
The hook exits with code 2, or returns permissionDecision deny in JSON, to prevent the tool call.
The hook exits with code 0 when it has no decision, so the normal permission flow applies.
An exit code 2 block holds, even when the JSON output says allow.
Hook scripts run outside the sandbox, so restrict their own permissions. (Inference)
pros: Adds a custom check that a permission rule cannot express.
Stops a call with exit code 2 before the tool runs.
Matches only the tools that a matcher selects.
cons: Each hook adds process time to each call that its matcher selects. (Inference)
Hook scripts run outside the sandbox and need their own review.
A script bug can block legitimate work. (Inference)
use_when: A team needs a custom check that a rule cannot express.
The check must run on each tool call that a matcher selects.
A blocked call must stop before the tool runs.
do_not_use_when: A plain allow rule or deny rule covers the case.
A person must decide in real time. Use pre-action approval in the session instead. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set hooks in managed policy settings, because user and project settings cannot remove them.
constraints.combination: Set allowManagedHooksOnly to block user, project, and plugin hooks.

constraints.choice: Log each hook decision with the tool name and the arguments.
Give the hook process only the credentials that its check needs.
Use a matcher so the hook runs only on the tools that need the check.
constraints.combination: Set a timeout on each command hook.

components.exam_tie: D5.3. Expect a scenario that needs a custom approval step. The credited answer uses a PreToolUse hook that exits with code 2. (Inference)
components.trap: A hook that prints a plain warning and exits 0 blocks nothing. To block, exit with code 2 or return permissionDecision deny in JSON.
components.decision_rule: Block in a PreToolUse hook with exit code 2, or with permissionDecision deny, when a custom check fails.
components.exam_tip: If a hook prints a plain warning and exits 0, expect the call to continue.

key_facts.text: PreToolUse runs before a tool call and can block it.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A PreToolUse hook that exits with code 2 prevents the tool call.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A permissionDecision of allow does not let an action through after an exit code 2 block.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Exit code 0 with no JSON decision means the normal permission flow applies.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The default timeout for a command hook is 600 seconds.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Hooks from settings files also run inside subagents.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: On PreToolUse, a hook that times out does not block the tool call unless onFailure is set to block.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: User, project, and local settings add hooks but cannot remove managed hooks.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Can the action be undone?} -->|No| B[Pre-action approval with full context]
  A -->|Yes| C{Volume high?}
  C -->|Yes| D[Sampled post-action review]
  C -->|No| E[Review every reversible action after it runs]
  B --> F{Custom check needed?}
  D --> F
  E --> F
  F -->|Yes| G[PreToolUse hook with exit code 2]
  F -->|No| H[Permission policy only]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  I[Irreversible] --> A[Pre-action approval]
  A --> C[Full context to reviewer]
  R[Reversible] --> S[Post-action review]
  S --> U[Tested rollback]
  V[High volume] --> M[Random sample]
  W[Webhook on idle] --> L[Scheduled session list]
  K[Custom check] --> H[Hook exit code 2]
